description:
Says why when ghostty-web fails to load, and xterm.js can take over. The test seeded a conversation at /c/gh-404, whose directory holds t.sh, which prints "xterm-took-over" and then echoes what it reads. The server answers 404 for ghostty-web. "The terminal" is '.terminal-panel-content [data-terminal-id][style*="display: block"]' and "the input" is [data-testid="message-input"]. To choose a terminal menu item, click the button with aria-label exactly "Terminal menu", then the button with exactly that text inside ".overflow-menu-panel" (two real clicks). "Read all output until it matches P" means: retry the following steps as one block until they pass (timeout 15s): fill the input with ""; choose the terminal menu item "Insert all output into input" (both clicks inside the block); the input's value must match P (eval with expect true). "Read the visible screen until it matches P" is the same with the menu item "Insert visible screen into input". "Set the theme to T" means what the theme menu does, the eval: localStorage.setItem("shelley-theme", "T"); document.documentElement.classList.toggle("dark", "T" === "dark"). 
1. Navigate to /c/gh-404. Fill the input with "!bash t.sh" and click [data-testid="send-button"].
2. The terminal should contain the text "Couldn't open the terminal". There should be exactly 1 ".terminal-panel-tab .terminal-panel-tab-error".
3. Choose the terminal menu item "Render with xterm.js". ".terminal-panel-tab-running" should be visible. The terminal should come not to contain "Couldn't open the terminal" (assert_text_not_contains).
4. Read all output until it contains "xterm-took-over".
